doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Music in childhood and getting a trumpet at thirteen
summary: Palmer knew only school singing until his father brought home a trumpet when he was thirteen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well when you were a young boy, did you grow up in Rome, New York?
Even before you started the trumpet, can you recall what kind of music you were hearing as a child?

No I couldn’t say off hand. Because my father brought home a trumpet when I was thirteen years old. So really just before that all I knew was singing in school, you know, school songs. But I liked music then. I didn’t care about singing that much, but you know, you joined in class vocals.
